<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is a standard, clean package definition for mpv-jamak. It declares a fixed version (0.4.1), downloads a tarball from the official GitHub repository with a pinned sha256sum, and installs Lua scripts and documentation via the package() function. There is no pkgver() function, no top-level command substitution, no eval, no base64 decoding, no curl/wget calls outside the standard source fetching, and no code that executes during sourcing. The source URL points to the project's own upstream (github.com/arrufat/mpv-jamak), and the checksum is provided (not SKIP, but even SKIP would be acceptable for this gate). Running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will only fetch and verify the tarball, extract it, and source the PKGBUILD to read metadata — no build-time or package-time code runs. This is entirely normal AUR packaging behavior with no supply-chain risk at this stage.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>Standard PKGBUILD with pinned source and checksum; no executable code at source time.</summary>
</security_assessment>
